key_insight: PoreML provides an end-to-end, pore-scale machine-learning workflow for learning and evaluating multiphase flow in porous media from large, physics-grounded simulation data.
engineering_relevance: It can accelerate design and screening for technologies where fluid displacement in complex pores matters, such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified training and evaluation for one-step prediction and autoregressive rollouts with physics-aware protocols
evidence_signal: The abstract reports five model architectures tested under unified protocols, plus two transfer challenges targeting larger domains and synthetic-to-micro-CT generalization.
watch_item: Performance may still be limited by domain shift between synthetic and real porous structures, especially when extrapolating to larger or less well-characterized geometries.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
